_note: What Mio, who keeps the fish traps and the old ferry on the river, says when the farmer talks to her (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction, gift_items her own answers to the moon lantern and to dishes. Mornings on the river she talks of her traps. The birthday lines (spring 12), the close lines from band 4, the ferry lines once her band 5 scene is seen (heart_mio_5), the dear lines at band 6 once her band 6 scene is (heart_mio_6) until she is promised; engaged_ lines once she said yes to the knot, and married (married_mio) help_ lines on a morning she did a chore, wed_morning_ / wed_evening_ at the farmhouse and wed_out_ elsewhere (data/marriage.json). Our own lines.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Petals on the river all morning. The fish think it's raining sweets.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: From the shore you see the fireworks twice: once up there, once in the water.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: On Moon Night the eels come up to look. Don't tell Kota, he'll try to catch the moon.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Last year's line, last year's knots. I cut them all tonight and start fresh.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Back again? Careful, the river will start charging you rent.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Still here? Grab a line, then. Talking scares the fish anyway.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Oh, the new farmer! I'm Mio. I keep the fish traps and the old ferry on this stretch.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: If you hear somebody laughing down by the water, it's me. The river's funnier than it looks.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Rain? The fish love it. My traps love it. Only my hair complains.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: The traps were full this morning! Well. Two fish and one very angry crab.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Mornings, the river's like glass. Step quiet or you'll crack it.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Winter traps freeze stiff. I break the ice with my heel. The river says ouch.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Hachiro thinks he's the best fisher in the valley. I let him think it on Sundays.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Sayo buys my catch every afternoon and haggles like it's a war. I love it.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Father built the hut from driftwood. Every winter it creaks a little louder. Like him.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: You know what day it is? Then I'm taking it off. No traps, no ferry. Just me and the far bank.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: For my birthday? Father always gave me a new float, painted red. ...This is better. Don't tell him.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: I left two river fish in your shipping bin. Don't ask how I got past your gate.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: You're getting a tan from the field. A river tan's better. Just saying.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: I oiled Father's pole again. Whatever the river decides, it'll be ready.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Kota asked if the ferry is a pirate ship. I said yes. Don't correct him.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: The boat has a name now. I say good morning to it. It doesn't answer, which is more than Hachiro manages.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Every morning I keep the first crossing for you. You never come. I keep it anyway.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: I caught myself humming at the traps. Hachiro asked who the lucky fish was. I threw a crab at him.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Tome has me scrubbing the shrine's water basin. She says I shouldn't smell of fish at my own wedding.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Hachiro says he's coming to the wedding to make sure I don't fish during it. Rude. Accurate.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Morning! I've been to the traps and back already. You sleep like a stone on the riverbed.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: The river's calling. Back by supper. The grill's mine tonight.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Your well water tastes flat after the river. I'll get used to it. Maybe.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Welcome home! Fish for supper. Surprise, surprise.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: I can't hear the river from here. I can hear you snore, though. Fair trade.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Married or not, the first crossing every morning is still yours. The offer stands.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: I watered the dry plots. Carrying water uphill instead of down. Strange feeling.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: The rows by the path were gasping like fish on a bank. Fixed it.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: The hens got their breakfast before you did. Don't be jealous.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: The feed's in the coop. Your sack, my arms.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Married life? Same river, same traps, a different walk home. A better one.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Sayo still haggles over my fish. Says marriage doesn't buy me a discount.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Oh! You know me too well. I'm keeping this all to myself.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Nice! Thanks, farmer.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Huh. Thanks. I'll find a use for it.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Hm. A bit too dainty for a river rat like me.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: A stone? I've got a whole riverbed of those.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Another? Save it. The river will think you're bribing me.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: You cooked this? It smells like Father's grill. ...Thank you.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Still warm! I'll eat it on the landing.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: A dish! Thanks, that's supper sorted.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: Too sweet for me. Kota will love it, though.

lines.speaker: mio
lines.text: A moon lantern! I'll hang it on the landing. Night crossings, here I come.
